```{python}
#| tags: [setup]
import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))
from _pcpkg import *  # noqa: F401,F403
import doe_report as D
import tables as T          # complex tables: merged cells, footnotes (T.<builder>(...).show())
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import scipy.stats as sstat

DOC = "PCP-003"
UO = "bioreactor"
UO_TITLE = "Production Bioreactor (Step 3)"

# --- doc-local derived scalars (pulled from the model; no number is typed) ---
import itertools, math, re
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

uo = CFG.unit_op(UO)
STEP = uo.step
HAR_STEP = CFG.unit_op("harvest").step
NAME = {p.key: p.name for p in uo.parameters}


def nm(k):
    """A parameter's name in running text."""
    n = NAME[k].replace("conc.", "concentration")
    return n[0].lower() + n[1:] if n[1:2].islower() else n


def nmc(k):
    """A parameter's name in running text, capitalized to open a sentence."""
    s = nm(k)
    return s[0].upper() + s[1:]


PCO2 = re.search(r"\((\w+)\)", NAME["co2"]).group(1)   # the short name inside the config label
assert PCO2 == "pCO2"                                  # the abbreviation the prose uses and defines


def nm_short(k):
    """The short name used after the first mention (pCO2)."""
    return PCO2 if k == "co2" else nm(k)


def g(x):
    return f"{float(x):g}"


def _days(a, b):
    return (pd.Timestamp(b) - pd.Timestamp(a)).days


num = T.num                      # numbers formatted as the complex tables format them
ATTR = {"afucosylation": "afucosylation", "galactosylation": "galactosylation",
        "high_mannose": "high mannose", "acidic_variants": "acidic variants",
        "aggregates_hmw": "aggregate", "hcp": "host cell protein", "residual_dna": "residual DNA"}

# revision, investigation and chronology
VER, EFF = doc_version(DOC)
V1_DATE = rev1_date(DOC)
_chron = csv("study_chronology.csv")
PLAN_KINDS = ["qualification", "screening", "univariate", "rsm"]
# The studies of this plan are the bioreactor studies that closed by the date of the Version 1.0
# reports. S-BRX-OSM and S-BRX-AUG came later; PCR-003 records them as discrepancies from this plan.
CH = (_chron[(_chron.step == UO) & _chron.kind.isin(PLAN_KINDS) & (_chron.end <= REV1["effective"])]
      .sort_values("start").reset_index(drop=True))
SID = dict(zip(CH.kind, CH.id))
_kinds = CH.set_index("kind")
FIRST_START, LAST_END = CH.start.min(), CH.end.max()
FIRST_CHAR = CH.loc[CH.kind != "qualification", "start"].min()   # first characterization run
assert V1_DATE < FIRST_START                       # Version 1.0 was approved before the first study began
assert list(CH.kind) == PLAN_KINDS                 # started in the order qualification, screening, univariate, RSM
assert _kinds.loc["qualification", "end"] < FIRST_CHAR      # qualification runs ended before the first characterization run
assert _kinds.loc["screening", "end"] < _kinds.loc["univariate", "start"]   # univariate starts after screening ends
assert _kinds.loc["screening", "end"] < _kinds.loc["rsm", "start"]          # response surface after the screening review
assert _kinds.loc["univariate", "end"] > _kinds.loc["rsm", "start"]         # univariate and response surface overlap
assert _kinds.loc["qualification", "end"] < _kinds.loc["univariate", "start"]  # set-point reference not run at the same time
_eqs = CH.equipment.unique()
assert len(_eqs) == 1
EQ_ID = _eqs[0]
_EQ = csv("dev_equipment.csv").set_index("id")
CAL_DUE = _EQ.loc[EQ_ID, "cal_due"]
assert (CH.end < CAL_DUE).all()                    # every window closed before the calibration due date
_ca = CAPA[CAPA.action.str.startswith("Amend PCP")]
assert len(_ca) == 1
CA_AMEND = _ca.iloc[0]["id"]
_pa = CAPA[CAPA.action.str.startswith("Record execution dates")]
assert len(_pa) == 1
PA_RECORD = _pa.iloc[0]["id"]
assert PA_RECORD.startswith("PA")                  # a preventive action of INV-001

# parameters and ranges
PP = plan_params(UO)
N_PAR = len(PP)
MV = [p.key for p in uo.parameters if p.study == "multivariate"]
UV = [p.key for p in uo.parameters if p.study != "multivariate"]
assert set(UV) == {"do", "ivcc", "medium_conc", "feed_vol"}
assert all(list(p.nor) == list(p.nor_characterized) and p.setpoint == p.setpoint_characterized
           for p in uo.parameters)                 # no NOR or set-point of this step changed at Version 2.0
assert all(p.prange[0] < p.nor[0] and p.prange[1] > p.nor[1]
           for p in uo.parameters)                 # range studied wider than the NOR at both ends
_ratios = [(p.prange[1] - p.prange[0]) / (p.nor[1] - p.nor[0]) for p in uo.parameters]
RATIO_LO, RATIO_HI = min(_ratios), max(_ratios)
DUR_SP = uo.param("duration").setpoint
DUR_UNIT = uo.param("duration").unit
MV_TXT = join_and([nm(k) for k in MV])
UV_TXT = join_and([nm(k) for k in UV])
RESP = list(D.responses(UO))
RESP_TXT = join_and([ATTR[r] for r in RESP])
# parameter names in running text, from the config labels (never typed)
N_PH, N_TEMP, N_DUR, N_OSM = nm("pH"), nm("temperature"), nm("duration"), nm("osmolality")
N_DO, N_IVCC, N_MED, N_FEED = nm("do"), nm("ivcc"), nm("medium_conc"), nm("feed_vol")

# designs
SCR_F = list(D.screening_factors(UO))
RSM_F = list(D.rsm_factors(UO))
SCR_ONLY = [f for f in SCR_F if f not in RSM_F]
assert SCR_ONLY == ["osmolality"] and set(MV) == set(SCR_F)
RSM_TXT = join_and([nm(k) for k in RSM_F])
LETTER = D.factor_letters(UO)
N_SCR = doe_runs(UO, "screening")
N_SCR_C = doe_centre_points(UO, "screening")
N_SCR_F = N_SCR - N_SCR_C
K_SCR = len(SCR_F)
FRAC_WORD = {1: "half", 2: "quarter"}[int(round(math.log2(2 ** K_SCR / N_SCR_F)))]
_scr = csv(f"doe_{UO}_screening.csv")
_fac = _scr[_scr.run_type == "factorial"]
_words = [len(c) for k in range(1, K_SCR + 1)
          for c in itertools.combinations(["coded_" + f for f in SCR_F], k)
          if _fac[list(c)].prod(axis=1).nunique() == 1]
RES = min(_words)
assert RES == 5                                    # the aliasing sentences below assume resolution V
RES_ROMAN = "V"
N_2FI_SCR = K_SCR * (K_SCR - 1) // 2
N_TERMS_SCR = 1 + K_SCR + N_2FI_SCR
DF_PE_SCR = N_SCR_C - 1
DF_LOF_SCR = N_SCR - N_TERMS_SCR - DF_PE_SCR
_rsm = csv(f"doe_{UO}_rsm.csv")
N_RSM = doe_runs(UO, "rsm")
N_RSM_C = doe_centre_points(UO, "rsm")
N_RSM_F = int((_rsm.run_type == "factorial").sum())
N_RSM_AX = int((_rsm.run_type == "axial").sum())
K_RSM = len(RSM_F)
assert N_RSM_F + N_RSM_AX + N_RSM_C == N_RSM and N_RSM_F == 2 ** K_RSM and N_RSM_AX == 2 * K_RSM
assert float(_rsm.loc[_rsm.run_type == "axial", ["coded_" + f for f in RSM_F]].abs().max().max()) == 1.0
N_LEV_RSM = int(_rsm["coded_" + RSM_F[0]].round().nunique())
N_2FI_RSM = K_RSM * (K_RSM - 1) // 2
N_TERMS_RSM = 1 + 2 * K_RSM + N_2FI_RSM
DF_PE_RSM = N_RSM_C - 1
DF_LOF_RSM = N_RSM - N_TERMS_RSM - DF_PE_RSM
for _d in (_scr, _rsm):
    assert sorted(_d.run_order) == list(range(1, len(_d) + 1))   # a randomized start order

# what Version 1.0 planned for osmolality, as the discrepancy that records the later osmolality study states it
_pd_osm = [d for d in PLAN_DISCREPANCIES.get("PCR-003", []) if "osmolality" in d["subject"].lower()]
assert len(_pd_osm) == 1 and len(_pd_osm[0]["studies"]) == 1
PD_OSM, OSM_STUDY = _pd_osm[0]["id"], _pd_osm[0]["studies"][0]
assert "screening design only" in _pd_osm[0]["planned"] and "held at its set-point" in _pd_osm[0]["planned"]
assert OSM_STUDY not in set(CH.id)                 # a later study, not a study of this plan

# univariate study and scale-down qualification
_uni = csv("univariate_studies.csv")
_uni = _uni[_uni.step == UO]
N_UNI = len(_uni)
UNI_REPS = int(_uni.replicate.nunique())
assert set(_uni.parameter) == set(UV) and (_uni.study == SID["univariate"]).all()
assert all(set(gg.value.astype(float)) == set(map(float, uo.param(k).prange)) and len(gg) == 2 * UNI_REPS
           for k, gg in _uni.groupby("parameter"))   # both ends of each range studied, replicated
assert all(r in _uni.columns and _uni[r].notna().all() for r in RESP)   # every response measured there too
_q = csv("sdm_qualification.csv")
_q = _q[_q.step == UO]
N_SD = int((_q.scale == "scale-down").sum())
N_M = int((_q.scale == "manufacturing").sum())
assert all(r in _q.columns and _q[r].notna().all() for r in RESP)
assert (_q.study == SID["qualification"]).all()
CI_PCT = int(round(100 * float(CFG.raw()["analytics"]["sdm"]["offset_ci"])))
ONE_SIDED_PCT = int(round(100 - (100 - CI_PCT) / 2))
for _r in RESP:   # the offset interval is Student's t with the pooled standard deviation of the two scales
    _o = D.sdm_offset(UO, _r)
    if _o["scale"] != "difference":
        continue      # a log-scale model (INV-002 CA3) is a discrepancy that PCR-003 records
    _a = _q.loc[_q.scale == "scale-down", _r].to_numpy(float)
    _b = _q.loc[_q.scale == "manufacturing", _r].to_numpy(float)
    _df = len(_a) + len(_b) - 2
    _sp = math.sqrt(((len(_a) - 1) * _a.var(ddof=1) + (len(_b) - 1) * _b.var(ddof=1)) / _df)
    assert abs(_o["half"] - sstat.t.ppf(0.5 + CI_PCT / 200, _df) * _sp * math.sqrt(1 / len(_a) + 1 / len(_b))) < 1e-9
N_COMB = 3 ** K_RSM
N_RUNS = N_SD + N_SCR + N_UNI + N_RSM
# the scale-down system runs several bioreactors at once: each study holds more culture days than its window
_CULTURE_DAYS = {"qualification": N_SD * DUR_SP, "screening": float(_scr.duration.sum()),
                 "univariate": N_UNI * DUR_SP, "rsm": float(_rsm.duration.sum())}
assert all(_CULTURE_DAYS[k] > _days(_kinds.loc[k, "start"], _kinds.loc[k, "end"]) for k in PLAN_KINDS)

# quality attributes
_cr = cqa_reg[cqa_reg.set_by == UO]
N_CQA = len(_cr)
NOT_RESP = [k for k in _cr.key if k not in RESP]
assert NOT_RESP == ["hcp", "residual_dna"] and set(RESP) <= set(_cr.key)
_CRIT = dict(zip(_cr.key, _cr.criticality))
CRIT_TXT = join_and([ATTR[k] for k, c in _CRIT.items() if c in ("H", "VH")])
VL_KEYS = [k for k, c in _CRIT.items() if c == "VL"]
assert VL_KEYS == ["acidic_variants", "residual_dna"] and _CRIT["hcp"] == "M-H"
_iac_all = D.iac_table()
assert list(_iac_all[_iac_all.cqa == "hcp"].sort_values("step").step_key)[0] == "protein_a"
assert "residual_dna" not in set(_iac_all.cqa)
assert cqa_reg.set_index("key").loc["fragments_lmw", "set_by"] == "harvest"
_frag = _iac_all[_iac_all.cqa == "fragments_lmw"].sort_values("step")
assert _frag.step_key.iloc[0] == "protein_a" and int(_frag.step.min()) > HAR_STEP   # from the Protein A pool on
_mp = csv("method_plan.csv")
assert not _mp[_mp.step == UO].lmw_in_scope.any()  # fragments are not an attribute of these studies

# intermediate acceptance criteria and their verification
IAC = D.iac_table(UO).set_index("response")
assert set(IAC.index) == set(RESP)
AV = IAC.loc["acidic_variants"]
AG = IAC.loc["aggregates_hmw"]
GLY = [r for r in RESP if IAC.loc[r, "basis"] == "drug substance"]
assert GLY == ["afucosylation", "galactosylation", "high_mannose"]
GLY_TXT = join_and([ATTR[r] for r in GLY])
assert float(AV.downstream_fold) == 1.0            # no downstream step is credited with removing acidic variants
TWO = [r for r in RESP if IAC.loc[r, "spec_type"] == "two_sided"]
assert TWO == GLY + ["acidic_variants"] and AG.spec_type == "upper"
TWO_TXT = join_and([ATTR[r] for r in TWO])
CHANGED = [r for r in RESP if bool(IAC.loc[r, "tightened"]) or bool(IAC.loc[r, "widened"])]
assert CHANGED == ["aggregates_hmw"]               # verification moved the aggregate criterion only
CHANGED_TXT = join_and([ATTR[r] for r in CHANGED])
# per attribute: aggregate tightened, then widened, net stricter than a priori
assert bool(AG.tightened) and bool(AG.widened) and AG.iac_high < AG.iac_high_apriori
# acidic variants: neither tightened nor widened, the a priori value stands
assert not bool(AV.tightened) and not bool(AV.widened) and AV.iac_high == AV.iac_high_apriori
assert AV.iac_low == AV.ds_low and AV.iac_low > 0  # the lower limit is the drug substance lower limit
assert all(not bool(IAC.loc[r, "tightened"]) and not bool(IAC.loc[r, "widened"]) for r in GLY)   # glycans unchanged
_ver = D.iac_verification()
BOUND_PCT = int(round(100 * D.VERIFICATION_BOUND))
_ver = _ver[_ver.step > STEP]


def _changed_by(cqa, kind):
    gg = _ver[_ver.cqa == cqa]
    gg = (gg[gg.met == False] if kind == "tight"                         # noqa: E712
          else gg[(gg.met == True) & (gg.widening_supported == True) & (gg.model_adequate == True)])  # noqa: E712
    assert len(gg) == 1
    return gg.iloc[0]


AG_T = _changed_by("aggregates_hmw", "tight")
AG_W = _changed_by("aggregates_hmw", "wide")
assert AG_T.step_key == "cex" and AG_W.step_key == "viral_inactivation"
assert all(int(x.step) > STEP for x in (AG_T, AG_W))   # no criterion uses data from the bioreactor studies
assert AG_T.predicted_nor < AG_T.assumed and AG_T.predicted_nor_bound95 < AG_T.assumed   # CEX cleared less
assert AG_W.predicted_nor < AG_W.assumed and AG_W.predicted_nor_bound95 < AG_W.assumed   # VI added less
assert abs(AG.downstream_fold - AG_T.predicted_nor_bound95) < 1e-3
assert abs(AG.downstream_added - AG_W.predicted_nor_bound95) < 1e-3
# acidic variants: the low-pH model is not adequate, so its bound does not replace the platform value
_av_vi = _ver[_ver.cqa == "acidic_variants"]
assert len(_av_vi) == 1 and not bool(_av_vi.iloc[0].model_adequate)
AV_P = _av_vi.iloc[0]
assert abs(AV.downstream_added - AV_P.assumed) < 1e-9 and float(AV.downstream_fold) == 1.0
# the arithmetic the text prints: drug substance limit x clearance fold - increase, from unrounded values
assert abs(AG.ds_high * AG.downstream_fold - AG.downstream_added - AG.iac_high) < 1e-6
assert abs(AG.ds_high * AG_T.assumed - AG_W.assumed - AG.iac_high_apriori) < 1e-6
assert abs(AV.ds_high - AV.downstream_added - AV.iac_high) < 1e-6
DOC_CEX = f"PCR-{int(AG_T.step):03d}"
DOC_VI = f"PCR-{int(AG_W.step):03d}"
# the platform worst case of the low-pH hold is an increase over a longer hold than the A-Mab NOR allows
HOLD_PLATFORM = int(re.search(r"(\d+) min", AG_W.source).group(1))
_ht = CFG.unit_op("viral_inactivation").param("hold_time")
HOLD_UNIT = _ht.unit
HOLD_NOR_HI = float(_ht.nor_characterized[1])
HOLD_RANGE_HI = float(_ht.prange[1])
assert HOLD_UNIT == "min"                          # the unit of the platform source text
assert HOLD_NOR_HI < HOLD_PLATFORM                 # the A-Mab NOR as characterized ends before the platform hold
assert HOLD_RANGE_HI == HOLD_PLATFORM              # the range studied reaches the platform hold
assert AG_W.observed_edge > AG_W.assumed           # at the edges A-Mab adds MORE aggregate than the platform,
assert AG_W.predicted_nor_bound95 < AG_W.assumed   # so the replacement reflects the shorter NOR hold
# the bound also covers the NOR in force: same longest hold and highest temperature, and no pH term
_vt = CFG.unit_op("viral_inactivation").param("temperature")
assert float(_ht.nor[1]) == HOLD_NOR_HI and float(_vt.nor[1]) == float(_vt.nor_characterized[1])
_vi_agg = [r for r in D.responses("viral_inactivation") if D.RESP_TO_CQA.get(r, r) == "aggregates_hmw"]
assert len(_vi_agg) == 1
_agf = D.fit("viral_inactivation", "rsm", _vi_agg[0])
assert _agf["status"] == "selected" and "ph" in _agf["factors"]
assert all("ph" not in re.split(r"[:^]", t) for t in _agf["names"])   # the selected model has no pH term

# the Version 1.0 limits
R1 = D.rev1_criteria(UO).set_index("response")
assert set(R1.index) == set(RESP)
K_SD = float(re.search(r"[\d.]+", R1.loc["afucosylation", "rule"]).group())
assert {r for r in RESP if str(R1.loc[r, "rule"]).startswith("mean")} == {
    "afucosylation", "galactosylation", "high_mannose", "acidic_variants"}
AG_MARGIN = float(R1.loc["aggregates_hmw", "margin"])
assert all(IAC.loc[r, "iac_high"] > R1.loc[r, "high"] for r in RESP)   # every upper limit is higher
assert float(R1.loc["acidic_variants", "low"]) == 0 and AV.iac_low > 0
assert all(float(R1.loc[r, "low"]) == float(IAC.loc[r, "ds_low"]) == float(IAC.loc[r, "iac_low"])
           for r in GLY)                           # glycan lower limits: the drug substance limits, unchanged

# the planned analysis
PAR_GRID_SP = D.PAR_GRID_SETPOINT
PAR_GRID_NOR = D.PAR_GRID
PAR_MC = D.PAR_MC_N
PI_PCT = int(round(100 * D.PI_LEVEL))
Q_LO = (100 - PI_PCT) / 2
Q_HI = 100 - Q_LO
SD_DIV = D.NOR_SD_DIVISOR
PCT_IN_NOR = 100 * (2 * sstat.norm.cdf(SD_DIV / 2) - 1)
assert all(D.decision_statistic(r) == "batch" for r in RESP)
ALPHA = THRESHOLDS["effect_alpha"]
LOF_ALPHA = THRESHOLDS["lof_alpha"]
GAP = THRESHOLDS["max_r2_minus_pred_r2"]

# tables built here and printed where they belong
_amv = dict(AMV_REFS)
_MAP = [("SOP-3010", "AMV-3010", ["afucosylation", "galactosylation", "high_mannose"], "every run"),
        ("SOP-3013", "AMV-3013", ["acidic_variants"], "every run"),
        ("SOP-3011", "AMV-3011", ["aggregates_hmw"], "every run"),
        ("SOP-3012", "AMV-3012", ["hcp"], "clarified harvest of every run"),
        ("SOP-3014", "AMV-3014", ["residual_dna"], "clarified harvest of every run")]
assert sorted(k for _, _, ks, _ in _MAP for k in ks) == sorted(RESP + NOT_RESP)   # the 7 attributes of the step
N_METHODS = len(_MAP)


def _resp_list(ks):
    labs = [ATTR[k] for k in ks]
    s = join_and(labs)
    return s[0].upper() + s[1:]


METHODS = pd.DataFrame([[_amv[a], s, a, _resp_list(ks), w] for s, a, ks, w in _MAP],
                       columns=["Method", "Procedure", "Validation", "Attributes", "Measured on"])
# the procedures and validations of Version 1.0: no fragment or titer method
_NOT_CITED = {"SOP-3015", "SOP-3016", "AMV-3020", "AMV-3021"}
PLAN_SOPS = [s for s in SOP_REFS if s[0] not in _NOT_CITED]
PLAN_AMVS = [a for a in AMV_REFS if a[0] not in _NOT_CITED]
assert {"SOP-3012", "SOP-3014"} <= set(dict(PLAN_SOPS)) and {"AMV-3012", "AMV-3014"} <= set(dict(PLAN_AMVS))
# Version 2.0 changes stated in Section 1.1
REV1_EFF = REV1["effective"]                       # the date the Version 1.0 title blocks carried
assert REV1_EFF != V1_DATE
assert PAR_GRID_SP != PAR_GRID_NOR                 # Version 1.0 stated the NOR grid for both analyses
COOK_RSM = 4 / N_RSM                               # the Cook's distance cut-off 4/n for the planned design
_osm_ratio = {k: (uo.param(k).prange[1] - uo.param(k).prange[0]) / (uo.param(k).nor[1] - uo.param(k).nor[0])
              for k in MV}
OSM_RATIO = _osm_ratio["osmolality"]
assert OSM_RATIO == min(_osm_ratio.values()) and sorted(_osm_ratio.values())[1] > OSM_RATIO
UNITS_TXT = join_and([f"{nm(k)} ({uo.param(k).unit})" for k in ("osmolality", "do", "ivcc", "medium_conc", "feed_vol")])
LEVELS = pd.DataFrame(
    [[LETTER[f], NAME[f], uo.param(f).unit,
      g(D.to_natural(UO, f, -1)), g(D.to_natural(UO, f, 0)), g(D.to_natural(UO, f, 1)),
      "screening and response surface" if f in RSM_F else "screening only"] for f in SCR_F],
    columns=["Code", "Factor", "Unit", "−1", "0", "+1", "Designs"])
KIND_TXT = {"qualification": "Scale-down model qualification", "screening": "Screening design",
            "univariate": "Univariate assessment", "rsm": "Response-surface design"}
_samp = [[SID["qualification"], KIND_TXT["qualification"], N_SD, N_M, f"{N_SD} runs at the set-points"],
         [SID["screening"], KIND_TXT["screening"], N_SCR, "–", f"{N_SCR_C} centre points"],
         [SID["univariate"], KIND_TXT["univariate"], N_UNI, "–", f"{UNI_REPS} runs at each end of each range"],
         [SID["rsm"], KIND_TXT["rsm"], N_RSM, "–", f"{N_RSM_C} centre points"]]
assert sum(r[2] for r in _samp) == N_RUNS
SAMPLING = pd.DataFrame(_samp + [["Total", "", N_RUNS, N_M, ""]],
                        columns=["Study", "Design", "Scale-down runs", "Manufacturing-scale batches", "Replication"])
SCHED = pd.DataFrame({"Study": CH.id, "Study type": CH.kind.map(KIND_TXT), "Start": CH.start, "End": CH.end,
                      "Equipment": CH.equipment, "Next calibration due": CH.equipment.map(_EQ["cal_due"])})
_CODE = {-1: "−1", 0: "0", 1: "+1"}
_TYPE = {"factorial": "Factorial", "axial": "Axial", "center": "Centre"}


def table(df, widths, fmt=None):
    """A flat table as a pipe table with fixed relative column widths (md_table), so that an
    identifier or a range is not broken across lines. ``fmt`` maps a column to a formatter."""
    fmt = fmt or {}
    rows = [[fmt.get(c, str)(v) for c, v in zip(df.columns, r)] for r in df.itertuples(index=False)]
    return md_table(list(df.columns), rows, widths)


def planned(kind, factors):
    """The planned design in coded units, in design order, as Version 1.0 gave it (no responses and
    no execution order). The coded columns follow ``factors``, the order in which the design lists them."""
    d = D.planned_matrix_df(UO, kind, coded=True).copy()
    raw = csv(f"doe_{UO}_{kind}.csv")
    assert list(d["Run"]) == list(raw["run"].astype(int))
    d["Run type"] = d["Type"].map(_TYPE)
    letters = [LETTER[f] for f in factors]
    assert sorted(letters) == sorted(c for c in d.columns if c not in ("Run", "Type", "Run type"))
    for c in letters:
        d[c] = d[c].map(_CODE)
    return d[["Run type", "Run"] + letters].astype(str)
```

# Purpose and scope {#sec-purpose}

This plan describes the Stage 1 characterization of the production bioreactor, Step `{python} STEP` of the A-Mab drug substance process [@fda2011]. The production bioreactor is a fed-batch culture with a working volume of `{python} f"{V['commercial_scale_l']:,}"`\ L at commercial scale. The step forms the glycan, charge variant and aggregate quality attributes of A-Mab (@sec-uo). The plan applies the strategy, the statistical approach and the framework of acceptance criteria of the Process Characterization Master Plan PCMP-001 to this step, following the approach of the A-Mab case study [@amab2009].

The studies are run in a scale-down model of the production bioreactor, whose qualification against manufacturing scale is planned in @sec-sdm. They cover the `{python} N_PAR` process parameters of the step that the Pre-Characterization Process Risk Assessment RA-001 brought into scope (@tbl-params). They also cover the `{python} N_CQA` quality attributes that the drug substance CQA register assigns to the step. Of these, `{python} len(RESP)` are responses of the designs, and host cell protein and residual DNA are measured on the clarified harvest of every run (@sec-cqa). The plan states the criteria against which each result will be judged and the analysis from which the proven acceptable ranges (PARs) of the step will be derived. The results will be reported in the paired Process Characterization Report PCR-003, which rolls up into the Process Characterization Master Report PCMR-001.

The characterization supports the transfer of the process from the development site in Cambridge, MA, to the commercial drug substance facility in Grafton, WI, under the Process Transfer Plan PTP-001. The results are the evidence for the operating ranges of the production bioreactor and for the part of the control strategy that this step carries.

Some related work lies outside the scope of this plan. The seed expansion steps that precede the production bioreactor are not characterized here. Harvest and clarification (Step `{python} HAR_STEP`) is characterized under its own plan, PCP-004. Fragments are not an attribute of the bioreactor studies (@sec-cqa). Confirmation of the ranges at commercial scale belongs to Stage 2 and will be made during process performance qualification (PPQ) at the receiving site [@fda2011]. The studies planned here are Stage 1 process design studies, and the claims they support are bounded by the scale-down model on which they are run.

## Changes in this revision {#sec-changes}

Version 1.0 of this plan was approved on `{python} V1_DATE`, before the first study of the step, the qualification study `{python} SID["qualification"]`, started on `{python} FIRST_START`. Version `{python} VER` is the protocol amendment that the QA investigation `{python} INV["id"]` required in its corrective action `{python} CA_AMEND`, which amends every step plan with the new criteria and the method for fragments. QA opened the investigation `{python} INV["id"]` on `{python} INV["opened"]` after its review of the master report PCMR-001 Version 1.0 for BLA readiness. QA closed it on `{python} INV["closed"]` with the classification `{python} INV["classification"]`. The investigation found that the criteria used to judge each step in the proven acceptable range analysis were in no approved protocol and had been set after the data were seen (`{python} INV["id"]` finding 1). The limits that the Version 1.0 report PCR-003 applied to the outputs of this step were among them. This revision makes the following changes, each set by the master plan PCMP-001 Version `{python} VER`.

1. Version `{python} VER` states an intermediate acceptance criterion (IAC) for each of the `{python} len(RESP)` responses of the step (@sec-criteria, @tbl-iac). The master plan PCMP-001 derives these criteria a priori from the drug substance criteria and the worst case of every downstream step on the platform (PCMP-001 §7.3). They replace the criterion basis of Version 1.0, an in-process limit derived from the nominal downstream clearance with a margin held between the two. They also replace the Version 1.0 analysis limits. For the glycans and acidic variants, the Version 1.0 upper limit was the mean plus `{python} g(K_SD)` standard deviations of the capability data that it was then used to judge (`{python} INV["id"]` finding 3). For aggregate, Version 1.0 carried the drug substance limit back through the nominal downstream clearance of this campaign and then divided it by a safety factor of `{python} g(AG_MARGIN)` (`{python} INV["id"]` finding 2).
2. Version `{python} VER` states the rule by which the verification of the platform worst cases may tighten or widen a criterion (PCMP-001 §7.5). That rule changed the criterion of this step for `{python} CHANGED_TXT`, which was tightened and then widened (@sec-criteria).
3. Version `{python} VER` judges acidic variants against both the lower and the upper limit of their criterion (`{python} INV["id"]` finding 4). Capability is reported as the lower of the two one-sided indices for each criterion with two limits, where Version 1.0 reported a one-sided Cpk. Capability is judged against a Cpk of `{python} g(CPK_TARGET)`, expected in routine manufacture, and a Cpk of `{python} g(CPK_MIN)`, below which an action is needed. Version 1.0 set no capability threshold.
4. Version `{python} VER` qualifies the scale-down model for each output by its offset from manufacturing scale, and it states every judgement against a criterion at manufacturing scale (@sec-sdm, PCMP-001 §7.1). This replaces the Version 1.0 criterion of no statistically significant difference between the scales at p < 0.05, and the Version 1.0 requirement to investigate a difference before any characterization run. Version `{python} VER` names the runs and batches compared. The decision whether the model is qualified for an output is made at analysis.
5. Version `{python} VER` states the campaign thresholds for model adequacy (PCMP-001 §7.2). The model F-test must be significant at α = `{python} g(ALPHA)`, lack of fit must not be significant at α = `{python} g(LOF_ALPHA)`, and predicted R² must fall short of R² by no more than `{python} f"{GAP:.2f}"`. The last replaces the Version 1.0 requirement that predicted R² track adjusted R². A failing model may also be refitted with a justified change of terms or transformation (PCMP-001 §7.2). The other adequacy rules of Version 1.0 are kept.
6. Version `{python} VER` states the tests by which the residuals of a response-surface model are judged (@sec-criteria). A regression of the absolute residuals on the predicted values, and a regression of the residuals on run order, each show no slope significant at α = `{python} g(ALPHA)`. No run has a Cook's distance above 4/n, where n is the number of runs in the fit.
7. Version `{python} VER` judges each quality attribute in the PAR analysis on the `{python} PI_PCT`\ % prediction interval of a single batch, which includes the model residual and the uncertainty of the fitted coefficients (PCMP-001 §6.4). The other factors are drawn from a normal distribution about their set-points and clipped to the range studied (@sec-par). Version 1.0 drew them from within their NORs and gave no interval.
8. Version `{python} VER` states the grid of the analysis at the set-points as the `{python} PAR_GRID_SP` points that the analysis uses. Version 1.0 stated `{python} PAR_GRID_NOR` points for both analyses.
9. Version `{python} VER` records the execution window of each study and the calibration status of the pCO2 probe that the studies used (@sec-schedule). The Version 1.0 records gave no execution dates (`{python} INV["id"]` finding 5). The Version 1.0 title block carried `{python} REV1_EFF`, the date on which the Version 1.0 reports were approved, in place of the date on which this plan was approved. The revision history now gives the approval date.
10. Version `{python} VER` gives the parameter names and units of the current configuration. The pCO2 parameter is named `{python} NAME["co2"]`, and the units are given in full for `{python} UNITS_TXT` (@tbl-params). No value changes.
11. Version `{python} VER` corrects the description of high mannose glycans in @sec-uo. They are the glycans whose processing stops before N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase I, not glycans on which processing never began.

The factors, their ranges and set-points, the designs, the sampling and the other decision rules are those of Version 1.0. The revision history also names `{python} INV2["id"]`, the investigation of the response-surface models that did not meet the model adequacy criteria of PCMP-001. The investigation `{python} INV2["id"]` changes nothing in this plan. What it changed in the analysis of the bioreactor studies is recorded in the bioreactor report PCR-003 as discrepancies from this plan.

The analytical method decision `{python} AMD["id"]` of `{python} AMD["date"]` made non-reduced CE-SDS (nrCE-SDS) the method for fragments at every step. The decision to measure fragments by nrCE-SDS does not change the methods of this plan, because fragments are not an attribute of the bioreactor studies (@sec-cqa). @tbl-criteria-change sets the Version 1.0 limits beside the criteria now in force. # Objectives {#sec-objectives}

The study has the following objectives.

1. To quantify the relationship between each studied parameter and each of the `{python} len(RESP)` modelled responses over the ranges studied in @tbl-params, and to identify the interactions between parameters.
2. To define the multivariate region of the response-surface parameters over which every modelled attribute is predicted to meet its intermediate acceptance criterion.
3. To establish a proven acceptable range for each parameter against each attribute whose fitted model contains a significant term in that parameter, and to confirm that the NOR in @tbl-params lies inside that range.
4. To provide the demonstrated effects and the operating risk from which each parameter is classified under the parameter classification procedure SOP-4001.
5. To provide the process understanding and the capability estimate that justify the Stage 2 operating ranges and the contribution of this step to the control strategy.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis {#sec-prior}

## Unit-operation description and prior knowledge {#sec-uo}

The production bioreactor is a fed-batch culture in which a recombinant Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cell line secretes A-Mab into the medium over a culture of about `{python} g(DUR_SP)` `{python} DUR_UNIT`. The pH, temperature, dissolved oxygen, pCO2 and osmolality of the culture are held at the levels of the run throughout that period. Each of them changes the specific growth rate of the cells and the rates of the Golgi enzymes that complete the processing of the antibody. The harvested pool contains everything the culture secreted during the run. A longer culture therefore weights the pool toward antibody made after the nucleotide sugar donors have been drawn down and after viability has begun to fall. The output of the step is the culture fluid at the end of the run, which passes to harvest and clarification (Step `{python} HAR_STEP`).

The platform on which A-Mab is produced was used for the humanized IgG1 antibodies X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab and for the A-Mab clinical and engineering campaigns [@amab2009]. Cell line construction, basal medium, feed strategy and the control of pH, temperature and dissolved oxygen are common to those products. The same host cell line carries the same glycosyltransferases and glycosidases, and the same medium and feed supply the same nucleotide sugar precursors. A parameter that lowered galactosylation in those products is therefore expected to lower it in A-Mab, through the same enzymes. The directions recorded on the platform are carried into this study as expectations, and the magnitudes are not.

Glycosylation is completed in the Golgi before the antibody is secreted. Protein A binds the Fc region outside the glycan, and the cation and anion exchange steps separate by net charge. Core fucose, galactose and mannose carry no charge, so none of the three purification steps retains one neutral glycoform in preference to another [@amab2009]. The distribution of the neutral glycoforms in the drug substance is therefore decided in the bioreactor. Sialic acid does carry a charge, and sialylated glycans are counted among the acidic variants. Aggregate and acidic variants are also formed in the culture, and the purification train can reduce that burden but cannot reverse it.

Core fucose is added by a fucosyltransferase from the donor GDP-fucose. The fraction of antibody that leaves the cell without core fucose therefore rises when the activity of that enzyme falls, when GDP-fucose is depleted, or when the glycan spends less time in the Golgi before it is secreted. Terminal galactose is added by a galactosyltransferase from the donor UDP-galactose, and both that donor and the manganese cofactor of the enzyme are depleted late in a fed-batch culture. Galactosylation is therefore expected to fall as the culture ages and the harvested pool accumulates late-culture antibody. High mannose glycans, mainly Man5, remain when processing stops before N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase I adds the first N-acetylglucosamine. Their level is expected to rise when transit through the Golgi is fast relative to the processing enzymes, or when those enzymes are inhibited.

The fucosyltransferase, the galactosyltransferase and the mannosidases draw on nucleotide sugar pools of limited size and work at the same Golgi luminal pH. Raising `{python} N_PH` or `{python} N_TEMP` therefore changes the rate of all of them at once. When a donor pool limits a reaction, a change that speeds the enzyme raises the product only as far as the donor allows. The amount by which one parameter moves a glycan attribute is therefore expected to depend on the levels of the others.

Aggregate forms after the antibody is secreted, while it sits in the culture fluid at culture temperature for days. A higher titer, a longer culture and a culture pH closer to the isoelectric point of the antibody each raise the aggregate level in the harvest. The isoelectric point lies above the culture pH. Raising `{python} N_PH` across the range studied therefore lowers the net positive charge of the antibody, which weakens the electrostatic repulsion between molecules and raises the rate at which they associate.

Acidic variants arise mainly from asparagine deamidation, with smaller contributions from sialylated glycans and glycated lysines. The rate of deamidation rises with pH and with temperature, and the time available for it rises with the `{python} N_DUR`. Sialic acid is added by sialyltransferases inside the cell, and glycation adds glucose to lysine residues without an enzyme, at a rate set by the residual glucose in the medium. These three routes do not respond to a given parameter in the same direction. The net direction in which a parameter moves the acidic variant level is therefore not predictable from the chemistry alone.

Host cell protein and residual DNA enter the harvest when cells die and lyse. Viability falls late in a fed-batch culture, so a longer culture carries a larger amount of both into the harvest. Protein A capture, cation exchange and anion exchange remove most of both.

A higher `{python} N_PH` raises the intracellular pH and with it the Golgi luminal pH. The glycosyltransferases and the mannosidases each work fastest at a different luminal pH, so a shift changes their rates by different amounts and moves the glycan distribution. A higher `{python} N_TEMP` raises the specific growth rate and the rate of every enzymatic and chemical reaction in and around the cell. A cooler culture grows more slowly and stays productive for longer, and a warmer one deamidates and aggregates faster in the culture fluid.

Dissolved carbon dioxide equilibrates with bicarbonate and lowers the cytosolic pH, so raising pCO2 moves the Golgi enzymes in the same direction as lowering `{python} N_PH`. Holding the culture pH at its set-point against that acidification consumes more base, which raises the osmolality as bicarbonate and sodium accumulate. An `{python} N_OSM` above the set-point draws water out of the cell, slows the specific growth rate and raises the amount of antibody each surviving cell makes. It also changes the size of the nucleotide sugar pools that `{python} N_PH` and `{python} N_TEMP` act on, so its effect on a glycan attribute is expected to depend on the levels of those two. A longer `{python} N_DUR` lowers viability at harvest and raises the fraction of the pool secreted after the supply of UDP-galactose and manganese has fallen. It therefore lowers galactosylation and raises the amount of host cell protein and DNA carried into the harvest.

`{python} nmc("do")` supplies the oxygen for oxidative phosphorylation, so a lower level slows the rate at which the cell regenerates ATP. The culture is not limited by oxygen at either end of the range studied, so neither the specific growth rate nor the glycan distribution is expected to move measurably across it. A higher `{python} N_IVCC` brings the culture to its peak viable cell density earlier and leaves more days in the productive phase before harvest, which raises titer. A higher `{python} N_MED` and a larger `{python} N_FEED` raise the supply of glucose, amino acids and nucleotide sugar precursors, which raises growth and titer. Across the ranges studied the feed replenishes those precursors faster than the cells consume them. None of these three parameters is therefore expected to move a glycan attribute at a fixed culture age.

## Quality attributes in scope {#sec-cqa}

@tbl-cqa lists the `{python} N_CQA` quality attributes that the drug substance CQA register assigns to the production bioreactor. Criticality was assigned in RA-001 with Tool #1 of the A-Mab case study, whose score is the product of the impact of the attribute on safety or efficacy and the uncertainty in that impact [@amab2009]. Criticality is treated as a continuum [@ichq8]. The levels run from very low (VL) to very high (VH), and the attributes of high (H) and very high criticality are called critical. For this step the critical attributes are `{python} CRIT_TXT`. Host cell protein has moderate to high criticality (M-H). Acidic variants and residual DNA have very low criticality, and their drug substance criteria still apply (PCMP-001 §3).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-cqa
#| tbl-cap: "Quality attributes that the drug substance CQA register assigns to the production bioreactor, with their drug substance criteria and criticality."
#| output: asis
show(cqas_for(UO))
```

High mannose carries the highest Tool #1 score of the step. High mannose species are cleared from the circulation faster than the fully processed glycoforms, so a raised level shortens exposure. Afucosylation and galactosylation are scored high because A-Mab acts mainly through antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity. Antibody without core fucose binds more strongly to the Fc gamma receptor IIIa (FcγRIIIa) on the effector cell, and a higher affinity raises the cytotoxicity that the bound cell delivers. Aggregate is scored high for its immunogenic potential.

Of the `{python} N_CQA` attributes, the `{python} len(RESP)` modelled responses of the designs are `{python} RESP_TXT`. The register states the criterion for acidic variants for measurement by CEX or icIEF, and this plan measures them by icIEF (@sec-analytical). Host cell protein and residual DNA will be measured on the clarified harvest of every run (@sec-sampling), but they are not modelled responses of this study. Neither has an intermediate acceptance criterion at this step. Host cell protein is first judged in the Protein A pool, and residual DNA is judged on the drug substance only (PCMP-001 §7.3). The ranges over which their clearance is controlled are established in the Protein A, cation exchange and anion exchange reports PCR-005, `{python} DOC_CEX` and PCR-008.

Fragments do not appear in @tbl-cqa. Fragments are formed in the culture and during the hold of the harvest, by proteases released from lysed cells that clip the antibody. The CQA register assigns them to harvest. Fragments have intermediate acceptance criteria from the Protein A pool onward and none at this step (PCMP-001 §7.3). They are therefore not an attribute of the bioreactor studies.

## Risk-based prioritization of parameters {#sec-risk}

The risk assessment RA-001 ranked every parameter of the step before characterization began. Each parameter was ranked on its potential impact on a quality attribute and on its potential to interact with other parameters [@ichq9]. Parameters ranked high, or with a likely interaction, were assigned to multivariate study. Parameters ranked lower, whose range could be supported one factor at a time, were assigned to univariate study (PCMP-001 §4). The risk assessment RA-001 gives the scores and the rationale for each assignment, and they are not repeated here.

For the production bioreactor, `{python} len(MV)` of the `{python} N_PAR` parameters were assigned to multivariate study and `{python} len(UV)` to univariate study (@tbl-params). The multivariate parameters are `{python} MV_TXT`. Each of them changes the Golgi luminal pH or the size of the nucleotide sugar pools, and the glycosyltransferases draw on both. The amount by which one of them moves a glycan attribute is therefore expected to depend on the levels of the others, and only a design that varies them together estimates that dependence. The univariate parameters are `{python} UV_TXT`. Each of them raises or lowers the number of viable cells and the amount of antibody they make, and the feed holds the nucleotide sugar precursors in excess across the ranges studied. None of them is therefore expected to change the rate of a Golgi enzyme at a fixed culture age, and a study that varies one at a time supports the range each of them needs.

The range studied of every parameter extends beyond its NOR at both ends. The width of the range studied is between `{python} g(RATIO_LO)` and `{python} g(RATIO_HI)` times the width of the NOR. The wider range bounds the response of each attribute outside the region in which the process should run, which allows the severity of an excursion to be assessed. It also sets the knowledge space within which a PAR can be claimed. No PAR is claimed beyond the range studied.

# Materials and methods {#sec-methods}

## Scale-down model and its qualification {#sec-sdm}

The studies will be run in bench-scale stirred-tank bioreactors of the same design class as the commercial production vessel, with the same control scheme for pH, temperature, dissolved oxygen and nutrient addition. Parameters that do not depend on scale, which include `{python} N_PH`, `{python} N_TEMP`, `{python} N_DO`, the `{python} N_IVCC` and the `{python} N_DUR`, are run at the commercial set-points in @tbl-params. Parameters that depend on scale, which include the agitation rate, the gas flow rates, the headspace pressure and the working volume, cannot be held equal across scales. They are set so that process performance at small scale matches performance at full scale [@amab2009]. The model is operated under the bioreactor operating procedure SOP-2003.

pCO2 is the parameter for which that distinction matters most. Carbon dioxide accumulates in a large vessel, because the depth of the liquid raises the hydrostatic pressure and lowers the volumetric mass transfer coefficient for carbon dioxide stripping. A bench-scale vessel strips carbon dioxide faster at the same gas flow per unit volume, so it reaches a lower pCO2 under the same nominal conditions. pCO2 is therefore controlled to the level of each run in the scale-down model and is studied as a factor in its own right, over a range that spans the levels the commercial vessel reaches. The carbon dioxide stripping of the commercial vessel is not matched, which departs from PCMP-001 §5 for this reason. The pCO2 of each run is measured by the pCO2 probe of the scale-down bioreactor system (EQ-BRX-205), which is calibrated and under change control (@sec-data).

The qualification study `{python} SID["qualification"]` follows the scale-down model procedure SOP-1001. It compares `{python} N_SD` runs of the scale-down model at the set-points in @tbl-params with `{python} N_M` manufacturing-scale batches of the A-Mab engineering and clinical campaigns. The comparison covers the viable cell density profile, the viability at harvest, the titer and the `{python} len(RESP)` modelled responses, `{python} RESP_TXT`. PCMP-001 requires the qualification runs to be made, and the offset of each output to be estimated, before the first characterization run of the step. The qualification study of this step ended before the screening study started (@tbl-schedule), and the report states when the offsets were estimated. A scale-down model need not reproduce the manufacturing mean. The difference between the two scales must instead be known precisely enough that no conclusion depends on its exact size. The model is qualified for each output separately, by the following rule (PCMP-001 §7.1).

1. The offset of an output is the mean of the scale-down runs minus the mean of the manufacturing-scale batches. It is reported with its two-sided `{python} CI_PCT`\ % confidence interval, computed from Student's t with the pooled standard deviation of the two scales. Each end of that interval is a one-sided `{python} ONE_SIDED_PCT`\ % confidence bound.
2. Every judgement of a scale-down result against a criterion first subtracts the offset of that output, in every study of this plan. Ranges and conclusions are therefore stated at manufacturing scale.
3. The conclusion for an output is whether it meets its criterion at all `{python} N_COMB` combinations of NOR low, set-point and NOR high of the `{python} K_RSM` response-surface factors. Each combination is judged on the exact `{python} PI_PCT`\ % prediction interval of a single run from the response-surface model.
4. The model is qualified for an output when this conclusion is the same with the offset at either end of its confidence interval.
5. An output with no criterion at the step, such as the viable cell density, the viability and the titer, has its offset recorded only.

The decision whether the model is qualified for an output is made at analysis, because the conclusion for the output needs the response-surface model. If the model is not qualified for an output, the report will state so and will state the consequence (PCMP-001 §5). The offset is estimated at the set-points only. Its use across the range studied is an assumption of this plan (@sec-risks).

The centre point runs of both designs are made at the same set-points as the qualification runs. They therefore carry the run-to-run variation of the model together with the variation of the analytical methods, and they give the pure error against which lack of fit is tested (@sec-stats).

## Cell line, media and culture operation {#sec-operation}

Cells are thawed from the working cell bank and expanded through the seed train to the `{python} N_IVCC` of the run. The production bioreactor is operated in fed-batch mode under SOP-2003, with a single nutrient feed added on the platform schedule. Culture pH is controlled by carbon dioxide addition and base addition, temperature by the vessel jacket, and dissolved oxygen by sparging and agitation. Basal medium and feed are prepared under the media and feed procedure SOP-2004 from the platform formulations. Each factor of a design is held at the level that the design gives for the run (Appendices A and B), and every parameter that is not under study in a run is held at its set-point (@tbl-params). The culture is harvested at the `{python} N_DUR` of the run.

Inputs that are controlled to a platform specification are tested for identity and quality on receipt and are not characterized in this study. They include the medium and feed lots, the gases and the base. Their specifications were set on the platform and are unchanged for A-Mab, so the variation they contribute is bounded by the specification and by the release testing of each lot. Where a lot of medium or feed is used in more than one design, its identity is recorded with the run, so that a lot effect can be examined if the data suggest one.

## Analytical methods {#sec-analytical}

@tbl-methods lists the `{python} N_METHODS` validated methods that will generate the study data. The released N-glycan map by 2-AB HILIC-UPLC measures afucosylation, galactosylation and high mannose from a single preparation, so the three glycan responses of any one run are not independent measurements. Size exclusion chromatography (SEC) measures aggregate as high molecular weight species (HMW). Imaged capillary isoelectric focusing (icIEF) measures acidic variants. The host cell protein ELISA and the residual DNA qPCR measure the two impurity attributes on the clarified harvest.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-methods
#| tbl-cap: "Validated analytical methods and the attributes they measure."
#| output: asis
print(table(METHODS, [22, 14, 16, 24, 24]))
```

@tbl-methods-by-study gives the method for each size variant in the two designs.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.methods_by_study([UO]).show()
```

Each method is used within its validated range and under its current validation report, and no method is modified for this study. Method precision enters the study twice. It contributes to the variation between the centre point replicates, and so to the pure error used to test lack of fit. It also sets a floor under the smallest change in a response that the study can resolve, so an effect of the same size as the method precision is reported as detected but not distinguishable from analytical variation.

## Sampling plan {#sec-sampling}

Each run is sampled at harvest, and the harvest sample is assayed for the `{python} len(RESP)` modelled responses. The clarified harvest of each run is assayed for host cell protein and residual DNA. Samples are taken by the procedure in SOP-2003 and are handled and stored in the same way across runs, because a difference in hold time before assay would appear in the data as a run effect.

The culture is monitored through the run for viable cell density, viability and the principal metabolites, under SOP-2003. These measurements describe how the culture progressed and support the investigation of any run that fails an operating criterion. They are not responses of the designs, and no model is fitted to them.

The screening design includes `{python} N_SCR_C` centre point runs and the response-surface design `{python} N_RSM_C`, all at the set-points in @tbl-params. The centre points are spread through the execution order, so that any drift in the medium and feed lots or in the analytical methods over the campaign enters the pure error.

## Statistical methods {#sec-stats}

The designs are generated, randomized and analysed under the design of experiments procedure SOP-1002, with the methods of the master plan PCMP-001 (PCMP-001 §6) [@montgomery2017]. Each factor is coded so that the set-point is 0 and the ends of the range studied are −1 and +1. A coefficient then measures the change in the response from the set-point to the end of the range, and coefficients for different factors can be compared directly [@amab2009]. An effect is reported as twice the coded coefficient, which is the change in the response across the full range studied of that factor. A model term is significant when its p-value is below α = `{python} g(ALPHA)`.

The screening data are fitted by least squares to a model of the `{python} K_SCR` main effects and the `{python} N_2FI_SCR` two-factor interactions. The model has `{python} N_TERMS_SCR` terms and the design has `{python} N_SCR` runs, which leaves `{python} DF_LOF_SCR` degree of freedom for lack of fit against `{python} DF_PE_SCR` for pure error. With so few residual degrees of freedom, R² describes the fit to these runs but overstates how well the model would predict new runs. The screening analysis is therefore read as identifying which factors and which interactions are active. It is not used to predict a response, to define an operating region or to set a range (PCMP-001 §6.2).

The response-surface data are fitted to the full quadratic model in the `{python} K_RSM` factors carried forward, which has `{python} N_TERMS_RSM` terms in `{python} N_RSM` runs. The lack of fit test uses the `{python} N_RSM_C` centre points and has `{python} DF_LOF_RSM` and `{python} DF_PE_RSM` degrees of freedom. Each model is reported with R², adjusted R², predicted R² from the prediction error sum of squares (PRESS), the model F-test and the analysis of variance that splits the residual into lack of fit and pure error. The residuals of every modelled response are examined against the predicted values and against run order, on a normal quantile plot, and as predicted against measured values. The response-surface model is the predictive model of this step, and every prediction, every PAR and the operating region come from it.

A factor with no term significant at α = `{python} g(ALPHA)` for a response is reported as showing no detectable effect on that response over the range studied. That statement holds over the ranges studied and no further. It also holds only down to the smallest effect that the design and the analytical method can resolve, which the centre points measure directly. An effect that is significant but small is reported with the predicted change across the range beside it, so that statistical and practical significance are kept apart [@amab2009].

A response-surface model predicts the mean response. At the edge of a region drawn on mean predictions, a single batch meets its criterion only about half the time if the variation is symmetrical [@amab2009]. For this reason each quality attribute is judged in the PAR analysis and in the scale-down qualification on the `{python} PI_PCT`\ % prediction interval of a single batch, not on the mean prediction (PCMP-001 §6.2).

Capability at commercial scale is estimated by simulating `{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"` batches (PCMP-001 §6.5). Each simulated batch draws the parameters of the response-surface models about their set-points, as in the PAR analysis (@sec-par), and evaluates the fitted models together with the variation observed in the study. Cpk is computed against the drug substance criterion. The criteria of `{python} TWO_TXT` have two limits, and the Cpk of each is the lower of the two one-sided indices. The same simulation gives, for each attribute, the probability that the drug substance falls outside its criterion. The variation drawn on is that of the scale-down model, which does not carry the contribution of the commercial vessel to batch-to-batch variation, so the capability will be confirmed against the commercial batches of Stage 2.

The set-point is the target at which the commercial process will be operated. The NOR is the band within which routine operation is expected to hold the parameter. The range studied is the knowledge space of this characterization. This plan assigns no parameter class. ## Screening design {#sec-screening}

The screening study `{python} SID["screening"]` varies the `{python} K_SCR` multivariate parameters in a two-level fractional factorial design. The design is a resolution `{python} RES_ROMAN` `{python} FRAC_WORD` fraction of the full factorial, with `{python} N_SCR_F` factorial runs and `{python} N_SCR_C` centre points, `{python} N_SCR` runs in all. At resolution `{python} RES_ROMAN` all `{python} K_SCR` main effects and all `{python} N_2FI_SCR` two-factor interactions are estimable clear of one another, and each is aliased only with interactions of three factors or more. Appendix A gives the planned design. The runs are made in randomized order under SOP-1002, which protects the estimates against any drift in the model, the feed lots or the analytical methods over the execution period.

The design carries no quadratic term, so it cannot describe curvature. A difference between the mean of the centre points and the mean of the factorial runs is read as evidence of curvature in that response, and the response-surface design resolves it. A three-factor interaction would mean that the amount by which one parameter changes the effect of another itself changes with a third. No such behaviour has been seen on the platform, and the parameters carried into the response-surface design are re-estimated there in a design without such aliases.

pCO2 and `{python} N_OSM` are separate factors of the screening design. The design therefore estimates the main effect of each and their two-factor interaction. In routine manufacture a higher pCO2 brings a higher osmolality with it (@sec-uo), so the combined effect of the two at manufacturing scale includes the interaction that the screening estimates. This plan does not state how `{python} N_OSM` is brought to its design level in a run in which pCO2 also varies, and the report states how it was done.

## Response-surface design {#sec-rsm}

The response-surface study `{python} SID["rsm"]` varies `{python} K_RSM` of the `{python} K_SCR` multivariate parameters in a face-centred central composite design. The design has `{python} N_RSM_F` factorial runs, `{python} N_RSM_AX` axial runs at the centres of the faces of the design cube, and `{python} N_RSM_C` centre points, `{python} N_RSM` runs in all. The axial runs sit at the ends of the ranges studied. A rotatable design would place them beyond those ends, at a culture pH and a temperature that the vessel control holds only with difficulty and at which the culture no longer represents commercial operation. Each factor is therefore run at `{python} N_LEV_RSM` levels. Appendix B gives the planned design, and the design supports the full quadratic model of @sec-stats.

The `{python} K_RSM` parameters planned for this design are `{python} RSM_TXT`. The parameter not carried forward is `{python} N_OSM`, whose range studied is the narrowest of the `{python} K_SCR` relative to its NOR, at `{python} g(OSM_RATIO)` times the width of the NOR. Its main effect and its interactions with the other `{python} K_RSM` are estimated in the screening design, and it is held at its set-point in every run of the response-surface design.

The subset above is the planned subset. The parameters actually carried into the response-surface design will be those that the screening analysis identifies as active on the attributes of @tbl-cqa. If screening identifies a different subset, the design will be amended before execution, the amendment will be approved by the functions listed in the approval record, and it will be reported in PCR-003 with the screening result that prompted it.

## Univariate assessment {#sec-univariate}

The univariate study `{python} SID["univariate"]` assesses `{python} UV_TXT` one factor at a time. Each parameter is run at the low end and the high end of its range studied, with every other parameter of @tbl-params at its set-point, and the harvest is assayed for the `{python} len(RESP)` responses and for the two impurity attributes.

This design cannot determine whether the effect of one of these parameters depends on the level of another parameter [@ichq8]. The range it supports for each parameter is therefore conditioned on the other parameters being at their set-points, and the report will state that condition wherever it states the range. The condition is accepted for these `{python} len(UV)` parameters for the reason given in @sec-risk. If a univariate assessment shows an effect on a quality attribute that this mechanism does not account for, the parameter will be carried into a multivariate study and the plan amended.

# Acceptance and decision criteria {#sec-criteria}

The criteria below apply the acceptance criteria framework of the master plan PCMP-001 (PCMP-001 §7) to the production bioreactor. Any change to them after execution begins is recorded as an amendment to this plan (@sec-approvals).

1. The scale-down model is qualified for an output when the conclusion for that output, whether it meets its criterion at all `{python} N_COMB` combinations of NOR low, set-point and NOR high of the response-surface factors, is the same with the offset at either end of its `{python} CI_PCT`\ % confidence interval (@sec-sdm). A model whose conclusion for an output changes between the two ends of the offset interval is not used for that output (PCMP-001 §7.1).
2. A run is accepted into the analysis when it was executed within the tolerances of SOP-2003 for the parameters not being varied, and when its harvest samples met the acceptance criteria of the analytical methods. A run that fails either condition is recorded as a deviation, investigated, and either repeated or dispositioned with a documented impact assessment. A study whose design is invalidated by a deviation is re-executed in full on material that meets the input specifications of the step, and the invalidated data set is retained and referenced in PCR-003 without being analysed.
3. A response-surface model is adequate for prediction when all of the following hold (PCMP-001 §7.2).
    a. The model F-test is significant at α = `{python} g(ALPHA)`.
    b. Lack of fit against pure error is not significant at α = `{python} g(LOF_ALPHA)`.
    c. Predicted R² falls short of R² by no more than `{python} f"{GAP:.2f}"`.
    d. The residuals show no pattern against predicted values or run order, and no single run dominates the fit. A regression of the absolute residuals on the predicted values, and a regression of the residuals on run order, each show no slope significant at α = `{python} g(ALPHA)`. No run has a Cook's distance above 4/n, a common screening cut-off for influential runs that scales with the number of runs n in the fit, which is `{python} f"{COOK_RSM:.2f}"` for the `{python} N_RSM` runs of the response-surface design.
    e. The normal quantile plot of the residuals shows no departure from normality.

    A model that fails any of these is not used to define an operating region or to set a range. It is reduced, refitted with a justified change of terms or transformation, or the design is augmented, and the revised model is reported with the reason for the revision (PCMP-001 §7.2). Where no adequate model results, the report states the response descriptively, against its criterion, over the runs of the designs.
4. An effect is significant when its term is significant at α = `{python} g(ALPHA)`. Significance alone does not make an effect important. An effect is practically important when the predicted change in the response across the range studied is large relative to the width of the criterion of that attribute. An effect that is significant but not practically important is reported as such, with both quantities given. Neither PCMP-001 nor SOP-4001 sets a numerical threshold for "large", so the report states the size of each effect against the width of the criterion and argues each judgement.
5. Each step output is judged against its intermediate acceptance criterion in @tbl-iac, at manufacturing scale, by the analyses of @sec-par. A quality attribute is judged on the `{python} PI_PCT`\ % prediction interval of a single batch. Afucosylation, galactosylation and high mannose keep their drug substance criteria, because no downstream step changes them. The criteria of `{python} TWO_TXT` are judged at both limits, and the criterion for aggregate at its upper limit.
6. An operating region is declared over the response-surface parameters where the response-surface models predict that every modelled attribute meets its criterion. The region is declared only over the parameters varied in the response-surface design and only within the ranges studied. The NORs must lie inside the declared region. If they do not, the operating region is reported as it is found and the NOR is narrowed until it fits inside.
7. A proven acceptable range is established for each parameter against each attribute whose fitted model contains a significant term in that parameter, by the analyses of @sec-par. A parameter has a PAR for each such attribute, and the range carried into the control strategy is their intersection (PCMP-001 §7.6). Where the analysis with the other factors varied across their NORs does not meet the criterion even with the parameter at its set-point, the report states that no PAR exists for the attribute and states the consequence for the NOR. The plan is met for a parameter when such a range is established and the NOR lies inside it for every one of those attributes.
8. The range of a univariate parameter is supported by its own data, with the other parameters at their set-points (PCMP-001 §4). A univariate result is judged by the rule of @sec-univariate. An effect on a quality attribute that the mechanism does not account for carries the parameter into a multivariate study.
9. Each parameter is classified under SOP-4001 from the effects demonstrated in these studies and from the risk that routine operation moves it outside the region in which those effects are acceptable, by the decision logic of PCMP-001 §7.7 [@amab2009]. A parameter whose variation affects a critical quality attribute is a critical process parameter (CPP) or a well-controlled critical process parameter (WC-CPP). The distinction between the two rests on the risk of falling outside the operating region, not on the size of the effect. A parameter that affects process performance without affecting a quality attribute is a key process parameter (KPP). A parameter with no demonstrated effect on either is a general process parameter (GPP). PCMP-001 and SOP-4001 set no numerical threshold for a high risk, a practically relevant effect or a wide PAR. The report therefore states the effect sizes and the margins between each PAR and its NOR, and it argues each class.
10. Capability is judged in the master report PCMR-001 against two values that PCMP-001 §7.9 sets. A Cpk of at least `{python} g(CPK_TARGET)` is expected of a critical quality attribute in routine manufacture. A Cpk below `{python} g(CPK_MIN)` requires an action in the control strategy. A Cpk between the two is acceptable, and the master report then states the side of the criterion that limits it and the parameters that drive it. The report of this step states the Cpk of each attribute with its margin to the limit and names the attribute whose capability is tightest.
11. The study is complete when the qualification of the scale-down model is decided for every output with a criterion, when an adequate model exists for every modelled response or the reason for its absence is reported, when an operating region containing the NORs is defined, when a PAR is established for every parameter and every attribute that its model shows it changes, and when every parameter of @tbl-params is classified.

@tbl-iac gives the intermediate acceptance criteria of the step and their derivation. Each drug substance criterion is carried back through the worst case of every downstream step, with no margin (PCMP-001 §7.3). The worst case is the platform value from X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab, unless the verification described below replaced it with an A-Mab value. The aggregate criterion is carried back through the aggregate clearance factor of cation exchange and the aggregate increase across low-pH viral inactivation. It is the drug substance limit multiplied by the clearance factor, less the increase. From the unrounded values in force this gives `{python} num(AG.ds_high)` × `{python} f"{AG.downstream_fold:.4f}"` − `{python} f"{AG.downstream_added:.4f}"` = `{python} num(AG.iac_high)`\ % HMW, against `{python} num(AG.ds_high)` × `{python} num(AG_T.assumed)` − `{python} num(AG_W.assumed)` = `{python} num(AG.iac_high_apriori)`\ % from the platform values alone. The upper limit for acidic variants is carried back through the platform worst case of the increase across low-pH viral inactivation, `{python} num(AV.ds_high)` − `{python} num(AV.downstream_added)` = `{python} num(AV.iac_high)`\ %. The lower limit is carried back unchanged at `{python} num(AV.iac_low)`\ %, which assumes that no downstream step lowers acidic variants (@sec-risks). Each increase is in percentage points of the attribute.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.iac_derivation([UO]).show()
```

Each criterion in force assumes that every downstream step performs at least as well as the worst case from which the criterion was derived. The report of each downstream step checks this from its own response-surface model, and the verification rule of PCMP-001 §7.5 lets the check change a criterion in either direction. Where the A-Mab worst case predicted within the NOR of a downstream step is worse than the platform worst case, the one-sided `{python} BOUND_PCT`\ % prediction bound of a single batch there replaces the platform value, and every criterion upstream becomes stricter. Where that bound is better than the platform value, and the model behind it meets the adequacy criteria of PCMP-001, the bound replaces the platform value, and every criterion upstream becomes wider.

The verification rule changed the criterion of this step for `{python} CHANGED_TXT`. The cation exchange model predicted a lower aggregate clearance within its NOR than the platform worst case of `{python} num(AG_T.assumed)`-fold. The one-sided `{python} BOUND_PCT`\ % prediction bound of a single batch for that clearance, `{python} num(AG.downstream_fold)`-fold, tightened the criterion (cation exchange report `{python} DOC_CEX`). The bound for the aggregate increase across low-pH viral inactivation, `{python} num(AG.downstream_added)` percentage points against `{python} num(AG_W.assumed)` on the platform, widened it (low-pH viral inactivation report `{python} DOC_VI`). The aggregate criterion in force, ≤ `{python} num(AG.iac_high)`\ % HMW, is stricter than the a priori criterion of ≤ `{python} num(AG.iac_high_apriori)`\ %. The bioreactor report PCR-003 argues the change by its risk, as PCMP-001 §7.5 requires.

# Proven acceptable ranges (planned analysis) {#sec-par}

A proven acceptable range is the range of a parameter over which the attribute in question is shown by supportive data to remain acceptable [@ichq8]. A PAR is computed for each of the `{python} len(RESP)` modelled attributes and each of the `{python} K_RSM` response-surface factors, `{python} len(RESP) * K_RSM` combinations in all (PCMP-001 §6.4). Each PAR is computed from the response-surface model of the attribute, with the offset of the attribute subtracted. The criterion is the intermediate acceptance criterion in @tbl-iac. Two analyses are run for each combination.

The first holds the other factors at the set-points in @tbl-params and scans the parameter of interest across its full range studied, evaluating the fitted response-surface model at `{python} PAR_GRID_SP` grid points. The PAR at the set-points of the other factors is the contiguous range around the set-point over which the mean prediction meets the criterion. This analysis shows what the parameter does on its own.

The second analysis varies the other factors across their NORs, and PCMP-001 calls its result the NOR-propagated PAR. At each of `{python} PAR_GRID_NOR` grid points across the range studied of the parameter of interest, `{python} f"{PAR_MC:,}"` sets of settings are drawn for the other factors. Each factor is drawn from a normal distribution centred on its set-point, with a standard deviation equal to the width of its NOR divided by `{python} g(SD_DIV)`, so that `{python} f"{PCT_IN_NOR:.1f}"`\ % of draws fall within the NOR. The draws are clipped to the range studied. Each simulated batch adds a residual drawn from a normal distribution with the residual standard deviation of the model, and it takes its own set of coefficients, drawn from the multivariate normal distribution given by the fitted coefficients and their covariance matrix. The `{python} PI_PCT`\ % prediction interval of a single batch runs from the `{python} g(Q_LO)`th to the `{python} g(Q_HI)`th percentile of the simulated batches. For an upper limit the `{python} g(Q_HI)`th percentile must not exceed the limit, for a lower limit the `{python} g(Q_LO)`th percentile must not fall below it, and for the two-sided criteria of `{python} TWO_TXT` both conditions apply. This analysis lets the other factors move as they move in routine operation, so the interaction terms of the fitted model contribute at every grid point.

In both analyses the PAR is the contiguous interval of the parameter, containing the set-point, over which the criterion is met. An interval that is met at the set-point but broken elsewhere in the range studied is reported as the contiguous interval, and the break is described where it occurs. Where the criterion is met across the whole range studied, the PAR is that range, and its edges are the edges of the study. The PAR with the other factors varied across their NORs is the one that supports a claim. It is in general narrower than the PAR at the set-points, for two reasons. It is judged on the interval of a single batch, which includes the residual and the uncertainty of the coefficients, while the other is judged on the mean prediction. It must also hold while the rest of the operating point varies.

The PAR of pCO2 is a range at the set-point of `{python} N_OSM`, because the response-surface model holds `{python} N_OSM` there. The offset brings the predicted level to manufacturing scale, but it does not carry the rise in osmolality that comes with a rise in pCO2 at manufacturing scale (@sec-screening).

The report will give both PARs for every combination in one table, with the range studied, the criterion and its basis. For each attribute the report will also plot the PAR of the factor with the largest main effect on that attribute, with the acceptable region shaded green and the set-point and the NOR marked. A PAR is univariate in the parameter it names. The operating region of @sec-criteria is the multivariate region over which every modelled attribute is acceptable at once, and it is not the product of the individual PARs. Where the two differ, the difference is the effect of the interactions, and the report will say so.

# Data management and integrity {#sec-data}

All data generated under this plan are recorded to the ALCOA+ principles. Run records are captured in the validated electronic batch record system under SOP-2003, and analytical results are reported from the validated methods of @tbl-methods with their audit trail intact. Raw instrument data are retained in the form in which the instrument produced them.

The designs are generated, randomized and analysed under SOP-1002. The design file, the raw response data and the analysis script for each design are retained together, so that every table and figure in PCR-003 can be traced back to the runs that produced it. Any exclusion of a run from an analysis is documented with its justification before the analysis is run again.

Instruments used to set or measure a studied parameter have their calibration verified before execution and confirmed after it. A calibration failure found after execution is treated as a deviation, and the impact on the runs performed since the last successful verification is assessed and reported. Each study record states its execution window and the calibration status of the pCO2 probe that it used, which the preventive action `{python} PA_RECORD` of the QA investigation `{python} INV["id"]` requires of every study record.

All data and analyses are subject to a second-person review before they are used in PCR-003. The reviewer confirms that the recorded settings match the design, that the reported results match the raw data, and that the analysis follows @sec-stats.

# Roles and responsibilities {#sec-roles}

| Manufacturing Science | Reviewer. Confirms that the scale-down conditions and the set-points represent commercial operation, and reviews the operating region against the control capability of the commercial equipment. |
