: Responsibilities of the functions that author, review and approve this plan. {#tbl-roles}

# Deliverables and schedule {#sec-schedule}

The deliverable of this plan is the bioreactor report PCR-003. It will report the executed designs, the fitted models and their adequacy, the operating region, the PARs, the capability estimate, the class of every parameter in @tbl-params, and any deviation or discrepancy from the plan. PCR-003 rolls up into the master report PCMR-001.

The activities run in the following phases. The parameters of the response-surface design are chosen from the screening result, so the phases run in this order.

1. Qualification runs of the scale-down model against the manufacturing-scale batches, and the estimate of the offset of each output. The output is the qualification record, referenced in PCR-003.
2. Execution of the screening design. The output is the screening data set and the effect estimates.
3. Execution of the response-surface design. The output is the response-surface data set and the fitted models.
4. Execution of the univariate assessments. The output is the univariate data set.
5. Analysis, decision on the qualification of the scale-down model for each output, capability simulation and parameter classification. The outputs are the operating region, the PARs and the parameter classes.
6. Reporting. The output is PCR-003.

@tbl-schedule records the execution window of each study, from the start of its first run to the end of its last run. Every study of this plan ran in the scale-down bioreactor system whose pCO2 probe is `{python} EQ_ID`, and every study window closed before the next calibration of that probe was due on `{python} CAL_DUE`. Confirmation of the ranges at commercial scale is not a deliverable of this plan. It will be made during the PPQ campaign at the receiving site under PTP-001 [@fda2011].

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(SCHED,
        caption="Execution window of each study of this plan, with the pCO2 probe it used and the next calibration due date of that probe.",
        label="tbl-schedule", merge=["Equipment", "Next calibration due"],
        header={"Next calibration due": "Next calibration\ndue"},
        align=["l", "P{4.2cm}", "l", "l", "l", "l"]).show()
```

# Risks and assumptions {#sec-risks}

The main risks to the study are the following.

1. The scale-down model may not represent the commercial vessel for an attribute it is used to claim. The qualification by offsets addresses that risk for the outputs it compares (@sec-sdm). The risk that remains is that the model represents mean performance without the batch-to-batch variation of the commercial vessel, and it is managed by confirming the ranges at commercial scale in Stage 2.
2. pCO2 depends on scale and is measured by the pCO2 probe of the scale-down bioreactor system (`{python} EQ_ID`). A drift of the probe between calibrations would move the true pCO2 of a run away from its design level, while the controller holds the probe reading at that level. The verification of the probe calibration before and after execution, with the impact assessment that follows a failure, addresses this risk (@sec-data).
3. Material supply. The studies need vials of the working cell bank and lots of basal medium and feed sufficient for both designs. A change of medium or feed lot within a design would add variation that the design does not model, so the lot is recorded with each run and lots are reserved for the campaign where the quantity allows.
4. Analytical precision. A response measured near the edge of its criterion carries the precision of its method into every conclusion drawn about it, and an effect smaller than that precision cannot be resolved by any number of runs at this design size. The report states the consequence wherever a range is set by a boundary that the method cannot resolve sharply.

The study rests on the following assumptions.

1. The platform experience of @sec-uo transfers to A-Mab. This is supported by the shared cell line construction, medium, feed strategy and control scheme, and the qualification runs test it directly.
2. The parameter list in @tbl-params is complete for this step, as the risk assessment RA-001 established. A univariate result that the mechanism does not account for would call it into question.
3. The attributes in @tbl-cqa are the attributes that the culture conditions change, and the attributes that the purification train removes are characterized at the steps that remove them.
4. The offset between the scales, estimated at the set-points, holds across the range studied.
5. Interactions of three or more factors are negligible, as the screening design requires (@sec-screening).
6. The univariate parameters do not change the effect of the other parameters within their ranges, because the feed holds the nucleotide sugar precursors in excess (@sec-risk), and their effects do not reverse between the two ends of each range studied.
7. No downstream step lowers acidic variants, so the drug substance lower limit applies to the output of this step.
8. In routine operation each parameter varies about its set-point as a normal distribution whose standard deviation is the width of its NOR divided by `{python} g(SD_DIV)` (@sec-par).

# Appendix B. Planned response-surface design {#sec-app-b .unnumbered}

@tbl-matrix-rsm gives the coded settings of the `{python} N_RSM` planned response-surface runs, in the code letters of @tbl-levels. The columns follow the order in which the axial runs vary the factors. The axial runs are set at −1 and +1, which makes the design face-centred. `{python} nmc("osmolality")`, code `{python} LETTER["osmolality"]`, is not a factor of this design and is held at its set-point in every run. The order shown is the design order, and execution follows the randomized order generated under SOP-1002.

```{python}

        caption=f"Planned response-surface design of study {SID['rsm']} in coded units.",
        label="tbl-matrix-rsm", merge=["Run type"],
```
